Hi Sergio / team,

Hope you're well — we completed a quantized build of Kestrel-7B-v2 (label: kestrel-7b-v2-quant) and would like Redwood to onboard it as an optional lower-cost variant for customers in the DL-8721 deal. The model owner at OpenModelHub has already published weights and permissive licensing.

Attached: kestrel-7b-v2-quant-eval-summary.csv (latency/cost/quality), and a short checklist we ran. Quick asks:
- Compatibility check with Redwood runtime (NV kernels + int8 paths)
- Any pinning requirements if we want the hosted API to fallback to kestrel-7b-v1 for regen safety
- Timeline for SOC2 evidence ingestion for vendor file (we can share a trimmed report)

Proposed timeline: aim to get it verified for internal canary by 2026-12-22 and public availability in early Jan.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Reddy
Procurement, Acme AI

Thanks Priya — and thanks for the evals. Looping internal owners. Short answer: we can onboard the quant variant, but there are three things we'll need before we expose it broadly:

1) Compatibility patch in the runtime for K-V cache alignment on int8 kernels (Dev, can you confirm ETA?)
2) A pinning/fallback policy so customers can opt to pin to kestrel-7b-v1 or opt into the new variant; for certain enterprise deals (DL-8721) we may need a temporary pin-exception until we validate production regressions
3) SOC2 evidence ingestion for the vendor pack (security team needs the trimmed report)

Action items:
- Dev: please run the compatibility script and share a compatibility patch + perf delta by EOD 12/17.
- Grace: can security accept the trimmed SOC2 doc attached, or do you need the full artifacts?
- Laura: product — if we do a pin-exception, can we ship behind a canary flag for Acme only? They prefer early access but need rollback guarantees.

I'll file INF-4392 for the runtime work and request a pin-exemption approval once we have Dev's numbers.

Best,
Sergio
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Quick update from runtime: we ran the compatibility harness against kestrel-7b-v2-quant on a 4xA100 pool and a 2xH100 dev pool. Summary:

- Baseline: kestrel-7b-v1 (float16)
- Variant: kestrel-7b-v2-quant (int8 w/ per-channel scales)

Findings:
- Inference path needs a small change for KV cache stride handling when using fused int8 kernels. Without the patch we see cache misalignment for very long contexts (~8k+) which can corrupt autoregressive continuation in ~0.4% of sequences in fuzz tests.
- Performance: int8 path yields ~1.9x token/s improvement for short sequences (<=512 tokens) and ~1.3x at 2k context when patch is applied.
- Accuracy: nll/regression tests show an average delta of 0.8% on our in-house eval set — within tolerance for a cost-optimized variant, but we recommend dataset-specific evals for Acme's critical prompts.

I've attached a small runtime patch (runtime-compat-check.patch) and the test runner logs. ETA: I can open a PR for the kernel alignment fix today; if we merge and run a canary we'll be able to sign-off on 12/21 for internal Acme canary.

Recommendation for pinning: because of the potential for long-context edge cases, request a temporary pin-exemption: host kestrel-7b-v2-quant behind a feature flag for the Acme DL-8721 tenant and keep kestrel-7b-v1 as the default. We'll lift the exemption after 2 weeks of canary telemetry without regressions.

- Dev

Thanks — that all sounds reasonable. Approving the proposed approach:

- Product agrees to canary kestrel-7b-v2-quant only for DL-8721 (Acme) behind a canary flag.
- We'll require an explicit pin-exemption request form to be completed by Acme (legal/procurement) documenting rollback SLAs and a 2-week telemetry window.
- Security: Grace, once you confirm the trimmed SOC2 doc is sufficient, please add the acceptance note to the INF-4392 ticket so we have an audit trail.

Sergio: please coordinate with sales/procurement to get Acme to sign the pin-exemption doc (I can draft a short template). Dev: please proceed with the PR and schedule an internal canary deploy on 12/21; if we see <0.5% regression and no long-context corruption in production telemetry, we can lift the pin-exemption on 01/04/2027.

Laura
